newsitem.title: USA: Sprint, Global One in global intranet pact.
newsitem.headline: Sprint, Global One in global intranet pact.

text.p: Sprint Corp. and its Global One partners, including Deutsche Telekom and France Telecom, said Tuesday they have formed a worldwide alliance to offer intranet services.

The services will allow multinational companies to employ Internet and World Wide Web technologies for use in their own in-house networks. The services are intended to create a "single, worldwide, multipoint environment for information sharing and electronic commerce," the companies said.

Sprint, Deutsche Telekom and France Telecom will market the Global Intranet to large, multinational corporations in their respective countries. Global One, the companies' telecommunications partnership, will market the service in the rest of the world, the companies said.
The three companies and Global One together carry the largest share of the world's Internet traffic.
Trials will begin with selected customers in the first quarter of 1997, and full service will be available in mid-1997.

Aviation, automotive, healthcare, publishing and technology companies are turning to intranets to speed up their services, cut communications costs, enhance communications among employees, customers and suppliers and increase productivity. A recent American Express/Harris poll of 334 top corporate finance executives shows that 61 percent are setting up intranets, Sprint said.
Sprint's stock rose 12.5 cents to $39.75 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
